Container.Name: Dropbox
Container.Overview:
Run the official Dropbox headless daemon in Docker. Built for reliability — handles large accounts (1M+ files), auto-restarts on crash, and stays up-to-date by pulling the latest Dropbox client on every startup.
Setup: 1. Install and start the container 2. Open the container log 3. Wait for a Dropbox URL to appear 4. Open the URL in your browser to link your account 5. Sync starts automatically
IMPORTANT: The Dropbox client does not support FUSE filesystems. You MUST use a direct disk path for your sync folder:
If your Dropbox share uses cache "No": /mnt/disk1/Dropbox If your Dropbox share uses cache "Only": /mnt/cache/Dropbox
Do NOT use /mnt/user — it will not work. The container log warns you if it detects this.
If Dropbox asks you to link again after every restart, put the config on a direct path too (e.g. /mnt/cache/appdata/dropbox).
Problems? Check the container log first: it reports a sync folder Dropbox can't write to, and where your account actually syncs to.
Open the WebUI for a status page showing sync progress, account link, memory and restarts.
Features: status page, process supervision, Docker HEALTHCHECK, JSON status API, Prometheus metrics, telemetry crash fix, graceful shutdown, large account support.
By Islam ElTayar — https://itayar.com
Container.Changes:
### 1.4.0 (2026-10-20) - Security: root never follows symlinks the Dropbox user could plant - Startup no longer downloads 90 MB just to check the version, and has network timeouts - Interrupted updates can't break the container any more - Keeps Dropbox's own .dropbox.cache; less log noise from "isn't responding" - Ownership repair at startup, on sync errors and daily, so array disks can sleep
### 1.3.0 (2026-10-11) - New status page: open the WebUI to see sync progress, account link, memory and restarts - Health check now turns unhealthy when Dropbox isn't running - Restart count and Dropbox memory are reported correctly; new Prometheus metrics - Ownership repair runs at low priority in the background
### 1.2.0 (2026-10-11) - Fixed: account links but nothing syncs when Docker created the sync folder as root - Fixed: Dropbox was force-killed on every stop or update with the template's polling interval - Fixed: several Dropbox processes started without the KILL capability - Fixed: crash loop on the very first start - Warnings for /mnt/user paths; new Ownership repair setting

Config.Name: Dropbox sync folder
Config.Description: Where your Dropbox files live. Must be a direct disk path (not /mnt/user).

Config.Name: Dropbox config
Config.Description: Persistent config and account data. If Dropbox asks you to link again after restarts, use a direct path such as /mnt/cache/appdata/dropbox.

Config.Name: User ID
Config.Description: UID for file ownership (99 = nobody on Unraid).

Config.Name: Group ID
Config.Description: GID for file ownership (100 = users on Unraid).

Config.Name: Skip permissions
Config.Description: Skip recursive chown on startup. Recommended for large accounts.

Config.Name: Startup timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for daemon initialization. Increase for very large accounts.

Config.Name: Max restarts
Config.Description: How many times to restart the daemon on crash before giving up.

Config.Name: Ownership repair
Config.Description: full: chown files in the sync folder not owned by User ID. group-only: only set their group. disabled: never change ownership.

Config.Name: Enable monitoring
Config.Description: Serve the status page and JSON API (port 8001) and Prometheus metrics (port 8000).

Config.Name: Prometheus
Config.Description: Prometheus metrics port (only if monitoring enabled).

Config.Name: Status page
Config.Description: Status page (WebUI) and JSON API. Needs monitoring enabled.
